text:
Situation: Cytarabine is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 25 vials of 100 mg/mL, 20 mL (8.7 days) and 45 vials of 20 mg/mL, 5 mL (14.3 days). Corvale General holds 67 vials of 100 mg/mL (24.5 days) and 127 vials of 20 mg/mL across two lots (18.3–26.8 days). Corvale Lakeside holds 15 vials of 20 mg/mL, 5 mL (15.2 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA's history shows a cytarabine shortage first posted on 2021-09-24 that has since been resolved. FDA inspection 1110628 at Gland Pharma Limited (FEI 3009056604) ended 2019-11-01 and was classified VAI, 693 days before the 2021-09-24 posting. The VAI classification letter is dated 2019-12-10, 654 days before that posting. Earlier inspections 848025 and 936901 at the same plant were also VAI, with classification letters dated 2014-03-21 and 2016-11-01.

Our position: No national shortage exists. Corvale East's 100 mg/mL, 20 mL supply is below target. Internal redistribution can close the gap without purchasing.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 16 vials of cytarabine 100 mg/mL, 20 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — raises Corvale East to 14 days; Corvale General retains 19 days. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
2. Substitute cytarabine 20 mg/mL from Gland Pharma Limited (alternate NDC) per prior approval by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2026-01-15. Approval: Pharmacist.
3. Substitute cytarabine 20 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. per prior approval by Alex Morgan, PharmD on 2025-10-06; requires pharmacist dose and volume verification. Approval: Pharmacist.
4. Purchase from Meitheal Pharmaceuticals Inc. if needed. Approval: Buyer.
5. Purchase from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC if needed. Approval: Buyer.

Not recommended: No action — leaves Corvale East below target.
